newsitem.title: USA: Brendle's to liquidate retail operations.
newsitem.headline: Brendle's to liquidate retail operations.

text.p: Brendle's Inc., which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in April, said Thursday it will liquidate all its retail store operations and begin close-out sales early this month.
Brendle operated its 58 stores as hybrid "showrooms" that offered brand name housewares, jewelry, consumer electronics and other products at discounted prices.

"Having given careful consideration to the company's performance since its second Chapter 11 filing, the Brendle's Board of Directors determined that there was no reasonable alternative remaining for the company except to discontinue its operations," the company said in a release.

Brendle's declared bankruptcy for a second time in April to implement a restructuring that included eliminating certain departments, closing 18 of the company's 30 stores at the time and renovating its 12 remaining stores.
The Elkin, N.C.-based company said at the time it expected the reorganization process "to be a relatively short one."
Brendle's had previously filed a Chapter 11 reorganization petition in Nov. 1992, and emerged from bankruptcy in April 1994 after closing 21 of its stores.
